key_insight: A three-miRNA myocardial signature (miR-517a-3p, miR-122b-5p, miR-4683) helped predict which aortic stenosis patients were more likely to achieve reverse left-ventricular remodeling after valve replacement, with stronger performance in women.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support pre-surgical risk stratification and identify patients most likely to normalize cardiac mass after valve replacement, while also pointing to potential biological targets involved in recovery.
method: Random Forest and Bayesian Network analyses were combined to select candidate miRNAs from LV biopsy sequencing data.
Selected miRNAs were validated by qPCR in an expanded cohort of 89 aortic stenosis patients.
Predictive performance was tested with bootstrap resampling, cross-validation, and sex-stratified modeling; murine TAC tissue was used for target validation.
evidence_signal: The signature showed good overall discrimination and achieved its highest predictive performance in women, with AUC values greater than 0.80.
watch_item: This is an early biomarker study with relatively small discovery samples, so the model needs external multi-center validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Machine Learning identification in patients with aortic valve stenosis of a myocardial miRNA signature predictive of reverse cardiac remodelling after valve replacement
